## Context / Problem
Three near-identical walkers discover a ticket's replacement link (iterate `deps` for `duplicates`, then `find_inbound_relationships` for `supersedes`): `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:58-108` (`_has_live_replacement_link`), `close_precheck.py:111-151` (`_recorded_replacement_target`), `src/rebar/_commands/close_disposition.py:76-118` (`find_replacement`), wrapped again by `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:166`. They differ only in liveness check and return type. Bug `frolicky-dependable-peccary` came from `verdict()` consulting only `find_replacement` while the "not_a_bug needs no link" rule lived in a comment in `_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked` (`close_precheck.py:169-174`); the `DISPOSITION_CLASSES == _NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` equality is held only by a test (`close_disposition.py:43`).

## Approach
One `close_disposition.replacement_of(ticket_id, tracker, *, require_live: bool) -> str | None`; `_has_live_replacement_link` and `_recorded_replacement_target` become one-line wrappers kept as monkeypatch seams (the 738a tests patch the boolean). `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` imports `DISPOSITION_CLASSES` so the equality is structural. Guard: the `duplicates`/`supersedes` walk (`find_inbound_relationships(` combined with `"supersedes"`) appears only in `close_disposition.py`.


## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_commands/close_disposition.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, `tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py`.

## Testing
Happy path: a duplicate with a live target closes; edge: a duplicate whose target is itself closed-as-duplicate is refused; not_a_bug needs no link. Pinning: `tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_disposition_69b9.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py`, `tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py` pass unchanged.


## The three walkers are NOT interchangeable — what the shared core may and may not absorb
Read of all three bodies before implementation (recorded so the collapse cannot silently change
behaviour):
- `find_replacement` (close_disposition.py:76) guards on `DISPOSITION_CLASSES` only and takes
  **no `ticket_type`**.
- `_has_live_replacement_link` (close_precheck.py:58) guards on `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES`
  **and additionally narrows non-bug tickets to `ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES`** (ticket fc20). It is
  therefore STRICTLY LESS permissive than `find_replacement` for non-bug tickets.
- `_recorded_replacement_target` (close_precheck.py:111) has **no class guard at all**, and on a
  failed `reduce_ticket` it **continues to the inbound pass** where the other two return early.
  Its caller pre-filters to `{duplicate, superseded}`.

Therefore the shared core is the **walk plus the liveness mode only** —
`replacement_of(ticket_id, tracker, *, require_live)` performs the `duplicates` outbound scan
then the `supersedes` inbound scan, applying `_is_live_ticket` iff `require_live`. **Class and
ticket_type filtering stays at each wrapper**, because the three differ there and merging them
would change which closes are exempt. The reduce-failure divergence is preserved by having the
core always continue to the inbound pass; the two live-mode callers are unaffected because a
failed reduce yields no outbound candidate either way.

## Rename hazard: the monkeypatch seams must keep their names
`_has_live_replacement_link` is patched with **`raising=False`** at
`tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py:94` and `:130`. With `raising=False` a
RENAME does not fail at patch time — it silently installs an unused attribute, and
`test_a_force_close_is_still_never_signed_even_for_a_linked_duplicate` would still go GREEN
while no longer testing what it claims. `_has_live_replacement_link` and
`_recorded_replacement_target` therefore stay as named one-line wrappers, and
`find_replacement` keeps its 3-positional-arg signature (patched at 738a:48 and
`tests/unit/commands/test_close_disposition.py:138,161`; called positionally at 738a:174).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The replacement-link **walk** has one body: the construct `find_inbound_relationships(` in conjunction with `"supersedes"` appears under `src/rebar` only in `close_disposition.py`, with a reasoned `# replacement-walk-ok: <why>` escape; checked by the guard test.
- [ ] Pinning suites pass with no assertion edits; checked by `pytest` and `git diff --stat`.
- [ ] `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (defined at `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:28`) is derived from `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` (defined at `close_disposition.py:44`) rather than restated, so the two cannot drift; checked by a test asserting the two sets are the SAME object, not merely equal.

## Review remediation (2026-08-21)
Three blocking findings on the previous ACs, all verified against the tree:
1. **The old AC1 was unachievable.** It demanded `grep -c "supersedes" src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` equal to `0`, but `supersedes` legitimately occurs there four times: `:67` (a docstring explaining the disposition), `:105` and `:146` (the walk itself, which does move), and `:186` (the user-facing remedy string `rebar link <replacement> {ticket_id} supersedes`). Only the WALK is consolidated; the docstring and the remedy string must survive, so a whole-token grep is the wrong oracle. AC1 now names the walk's constituent conjunction, per the parent epic's guard rule #2.
2. **The old AC3 named the wrong file.** It said `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` is "checked by reading `txn.py`"; that constant is defined at `close_precheck.py:28` and does not appear in `txn.py`. AC3 now names both real locations.
3. **"Checked by reading" is not a check.** AC3 now requires an identity assertion (same object), which is what actually prevents the two sets drifting apart — the drift that bug `frolicky-dependable-peccary` came from.
- [ ] The non-bug ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES narrowing that only `_has_live_replacement_link` applies is preserved; checked by a test closing a non-bug ticket as `not_a_bug` and asserting the exemption is still refused.
- [ ] `_has_live_replacement_link`, `_recorded_replacement_target` and `find_replacement` keep their exact names and signatures as monkeypatch seams; checked by a test that patches each by name with `raising=True`.
